intro: These are the same priorities I ran on in 2023. They still guide every vote I take.

items.title: Attainable housing
items.summary: Homes that young families, seniors and workers can actually afford, while limiting sprawl into farmland and foothills.
items.next: Build on River Crossing with more income-qualified homes to buy, and keep student housing near campus so single-family homes stay available for families.

items.title: Fiscal responsibility
items.summary: A balanced budget, careful spending and no waste. Every tax dollar should do real work for Logan.
items.next: Keep core services strong (police, fire, roads, water) and look hard at anything that isn't.

items.title: Traffic, walking & biking
items.summary: Streets that work for everyone, whether you drive, walk, bike or push a stroller: safer crossings, connected bike lanes and sidewalks, and smarter roads to ease congestion.
items.next: Finish Logan's new active transportation master plan and launch a transportation board made up of community members, so residents have a direct voice in how our streets are designed.

items.title: Parks, trails & a new rec center
items.summary: More parks, trails and places to gather, plus support for the small businesses that make downtown a place people want to be.
items.next: Finish the "Logan Greenway", a continuous trail connecting First Dam to Trapper Park, and build a new recreation center for Logan.

items.title: Quality local jobs
items.summary: Support for local businesses, entrepreneurs and higher-paying jobs so our kids can build a life here.
items.next: Make it simpler to start and grow a small business in Logan.

items.title: Long-term vision
items.summary: Plan roads, housing and businesses for the next generation, not just the next election.
items.next: Put the Logan 2045 General Plan to work, one zoning decision at a time.
